observations.seen: Warm low sunset key from behind the track gives a pleasant pink/gold mood, but the track surface reads flat and evenly lit. A blown yellow hotspot sits mid-track. This is a dusk look, not the recipe's outdoor-day 3/4 front sun.

Gates cast soft, readable shadows across the track, and the ball has a contact shadow. Distant wooden spires and floating islands show little self-shadowing, and the rail beads cast no visible ground shadow.

The red ball relies on a painted-style white highlight and rim rather than reflecting the sky. The rail beads carry a generic specular dot. There is no visible environment reflection of the pink sky on glossy surfaces.

The dripping paint gates and glossy ball read well. The track wood texture is low-contrast and washed out. The spires are flat-shaded brown, and the clouds are flat cutout-like shapes with simple two-tone shading.

The camera is a low chase cam directly behind the ball, not the recipe's side-on follow. In frames 1 and 2 the ball fills roughly 20% of the frame and occludes the gate it is about to pass. In frame 4 it is small and centered, so framing is inconsistent.

Bloom is pushed hard where the track meets the horizon, creating a yellow glare band that flattens detail. White speed-line streaks scratched across the sky look like artifacts rather than motion blur.
Only motion cues are visible: the paint splatter trail behind the ball, flying droplets at the gate, and speed streaks. Rolling or squash motion cannot be confirmed from stills.

The world is cohesive: floating grass islands with towers, hot-air balloons, bunting flags, tall wooden spires and a cloud sea. The palette is pink/purple dusk instead of the saturated greens and sky blue the recipe calls for.
Distance haze fades the far spires and curving track into pink. The fog density is reasonable, though the sky gradient dominates the haze color.

nextChange.change: set the look's environment so metals/glossy materials pick up image-based reflections
